title: UNIQUE constraint (ALTER TABLE)
description: You can add a constraint to a table that already exists with ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT, not just when you first create it. Add a UNIQUE constraint named `products_name_unique` on the `products.name` column.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: ADD CONSTRAINT, UNIQUE
ADD CONSTRAINT <constraint_name> UNIQUE (<column>) is the general pattern - the constraint needs its own name so Postgres has something to report if a future INSERT ever violates it.
Target the products table, give the constraint the exact name products_name_unique, and make it UNIQUE on the name column.
expected_behavior: products.name can no longer contain duplicate values - a future INSERT reusing an existing name would be rejected.
solution: ALTER TABLE products ADD CONSTRAINT products_name_unique UNIQUE (name);
explanation: Constraints don't have to be decided up front at CREATE TABLE time - real schemas evolve, and ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT is how you tighten the rules on a table that's already live.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT constraint_type FROM information_schema.table_constraints WHERE table_schema = 'fixtures' AND table_name = 'products' AND constraint_name = 'products_name_unique'
hidden_tests.label: products_name_unique constraint exists
